title: DeckTalk project file
description: Every table of a DeckTalk project file. A document table says what the film is and a tuning table says how it is made, and each key publishes the range that is safe to turn it through.

video.description: These keys set the frame size and the encoding of every recording and of the final mp4.

width.description: Frame width in pixels, for every recording and the final mp4.

height.description: Frame height in pixels, for every recording and the final mp4.

output_fps.description: Frame rate of the final mp4. The recorder's own rate is measured and is not a knob.
output_fps.x-hazard: Encoding below the rate the recorder captured at drops presented frames, which both loses motion a viewer saw and corrupts the frames verify measures its own verdicts from.

preset.description: x264 preset. Use veryfast for drafts.
preset.x-range: must be one of ultrafast, superfast, veryfast, faster, fast, medium, slow, slower, veryslow

crf.description: x264 quality. A lower value gives higher quality and a larger file.
crf.x-hazard: Above about 32 the encoder's own ringing is larger than a small reveal, so a cue that played reads as no change and the check that would have caught it passes instead.

audio_bitrate.description: AAC bitrate of the final mp4.

sample_rate.description: Audio sample rate of the final mp4. Every audio input is resampled to it once.

channels.description: Audio channels of the final mp4.

slate_color.description: Color of the plain frame that plays when a slate image cannot be rendered.
slate_color.x-range: takes any value of its type

narration.description: These keys govern how the script is turned into audio.

model.description: Speech model. `[voice] model` and `--set narration.model` override it.
model.x-range: takes any value of its type

output_format.description: Audio format that the speech provider returns. It is part of the narration cache key.
output_format.x-range: takes any value of its type

mp3_bitrate.description: Bitrate of the mp3 files that DeckTalk writes, which are the click tracks and the joined narration.

words_per_minute.description: Pacing of the estimated length in the narrate table.

silent_words_per_minute.description: Pacing of the click track in a build without voice.

lead_seconds.description: Silence before the first word of every spoken section, so the picture changes before the voice speaks. A section's own `lead_seconds` replaces it.

silent_beat_seconds.description: Seconds each beat adds to a section's length in a build without voice.

tail_min_seconds.description: Silence after the last word of every spoken section, so a cut never falls on speech. The take is placed so that exactly this much follows its last sound. A section's own `tail_seconds` replaces it.

cache_dir.description: Directory that holds the take files and their words files, each named by its content hash. It is empty for `build/narrate/` inside the project, and a path here keeps the voiced takes when `build/` is deleted and lets many projects share one cache.
cache_dir.x-range: takes any value of its type

context_chars.description: Characters of each neighbour section sent with a request, for continuous prosody.

timeout_seconds.description: Seconds before a speech request times out.

sound_end_noise_dbfs.description: Level under which the tail of a take counts as silence, which is where the take's sound ends.
sound_end_noise_dbfs.x-hazard: Above about -25 dBFS the scan calls quiet speech silence, so the take is placed early and the cut that follows it lands on a word.

sound_end_min_run_seconds.description: Shortest run under the noise level that counts as the end of a take's sound.

record.description: These keys tune the headless Chromium recording and how narration t=0 is found in it.

settle_seconds.description: Shortest wait after the page is ready and before narration t=0.

min_cover_seconds.description: Shortest time from the start of the recorder to narration t=0.

browser_path.description: Chromium executable that `record` drives. It is empty for the build DeckTalk fetches itself, and a path here is what a managed machine sets: a named executable that will not launch is never a reason to download another.
browser_path.x-range: takes any value of its type

color_scheme.description: Color scheme that Chromium reports to the page.
color_scheme.x-range: must be one of light, dark, no-preference

retries.description: How many more times `record` records a section whose frames stalled.

screenshot_settle_seconds.description: Seconds that `storyboard` waits before each slide panel.

cover_scan_seconds.description: Seconds at the start of each recording that `record` scans for the magenta cover.

fallback_first_paint_seconds.description: Guessed first paint when `record` finds no cover and no painted frame. `record` adds `settle_seconds` to it.

cover_luma_min.description: A cover frame has an average luma above this.

cover_luma_max.description: A cover frame has an average luma below this.

cover_chroma_min.description: A cover frame has an average U and an average V above this.

painted_peak_luma_min.description: A painted frame has a brightest luma above this.

painted_mean_luma_max.description: A painted frame has an average luma below this, so a white flash does not count as the picture.

truncated_slack_seconds.description: Allowed shortfall of a recording against its requested length.

frame_gap_max_ms.description: Longest gap between two presented frames after narration t=0. A longer gap makes `record` try again.
frame_gap_max_ms.x-hazard: The runtime reports a gap no finer than its own reporting floor, so a limit under that floor makes every section stall and every retry spend the recording again.

audio.description: These keys set the mix mechanics. Levels are project content and live in `[mix]`.

duck_ramp_seconds.description: Ramp of the music duck at each edge of a spoken span or a clip.

ambience_ramp_seconds.description: Ramp of the ambience bed at each edge of its span.

ambience_pad_seconds.description: Seconds that the ambience bed extends past each edge of its section.

marker_mute_ramp_seconds.description: Ramp into and out of a marker's mute.

marker_boost_ramp_seconds.description: Ramp into and out of a marker's swell.

verify.description: These keys are the limits `verify` judges the assembled mp4 against.

after_dip_seconds.description: Seconds after a section start to the frame that the start check reads.

reference_lead_extra_ms.description: Extra lead added to the reference frame beyond the one the offset limit implies.
reference_lead_extra_ms.x-hazard: The lead is already the offset limit plus the grid guard, so extra lead is only ever the escape hatch for a deck whose reference frame is still inside its own reveal. Above about 80 milliseconds the reference frame reaches back into the previous cue and the check compares two changes rather than one.

probe_delays_seconds.description: Seconds after the cue time for each probe. The later probe catches a slow reveal.
probe_delays_seconds.x-range: must hold at least 1 and must hold values that each must be above 0 and must be at most 10

probe_diff_luma.description: Luma difference a pixel must exceed to count as changed, for the probes and the control shares.
probe_diff_luma.x-hazard: A high value counts only a change that crosses most of the range, so a reveal that fades in or moves a light element on a light slide reads as no change at all.

changed_share_min_percent.description: Smallest share of the frame, in percent, that the reported probe must find changed.
changed_share_min_percent.x-hazard: Above about 5 percent only a change across most of the slide passes, so every small reveal in the deck reports a failure it cannot fix.

margin_min_points.description: Smallest margin, in percentage points, between the reported probe and its control.

thin_change_factor.description: A passing cue whose changed share or margin is under this many times its floor is uncertain rather than clean. A value of 1 turns that second opinion off.

onset_rise_points.description: Rise in the changed share from one frame to the next that marks the onset, in percentage points.
onset_rise_points.x-hazard: The rise is measured over a quarter-size frame, so one point is already tens of thousands of pixels. Above about one point no frame ever qualifies, every cue reports a null offset, and the check that names a late reveal stops running while the run still exits clean.

onset_diff_luma.description: Luma difference a pixel must exceed to count as changed, for the onset scan alone.

click_search_seconds.description: Seconds on each side of the cued word's start that the click search covers.

click_floor_dbfs.description: Level a sample must exceed for the click search to call it the click.
click_floor_dbfs.x-hazard: DeckTalk generates its own click at -24 dBFS, so a floor at or above that level finds no click at all and every a/v row measures nothing while reporting no failure.

cue_offset_max_ms.description: How far the measured onset may sit from the cue time, early or late.
cue_offset_max_ms.x-hazard: A viewer sees a reveal land late at about a fifth of a second, so above roughly 200 milliseconds the limit passes films whose pictures visibly miss their words.

av_offset_max_ms.description: How far the click may sit from the word it marks, early or late. It is wider than the cue limit because the click carries the encoder's own jitter as well.
av_offset_max_ms.x-hazard: An mp3 frame smears a transient across about 26 milliseconds and the encode adds its own, so a limit under 80 milliseconds reports a failure that no edit to the film can clear.

black_max_luma.description: A frame whose brightest luma is at most this is black, whether `record` or `verify` reads it.

cut_window_seconds.description: Seconds of narration before each cut that the cut check measures.

cut_max_dbfs.description: Loudest level the cut window may reach before the cut counts as falling on speech.

cut_change_max_percent.description: Largest share of the frame, in percent, that may change across a cut into a seamless section.

voice.description: These keys are what the speech provider is asked for and what its characters cost.

stability.description: How closely the voice holds one delivery across takes.
stability.x-hazard: The provider takes a share and refuses anything else, so a value read as a percentage fails the request rather than the load.

similarity_boost.description: How closely the voice holds to the original recording it was cloned from.

style.description: How much expressive style the voice adds beyond the words.

speaker_boost.description: Whether the provider applies its own speaker boost to the take.
speaker_boost.x-range: takes any value of its type

speed.description: How fast the voice speaks, as a multiple of its natural pace.
speed.x-hazard: The provider refuses a multiple outside its own range, so a slower read is a script change rather than a knob.

price_per_1000_characters.description: What this project's plan charges per thousand characters of speech.
price_per_1000_characters.x-evidence: the plan page of the account whose key this project uses
price_per_1000_characters.x-hazard: It is zero until somebody states it, and a spend cap refuses a run while the price is still the default, because DeckTalk would otherwise be capping a spend against a number it invented.

mix.description: The tuning half of `[mix]`. The music, the ambience and the levels are project content.

loudness.description: These keys are the programme loudness the final mp4 is normalised to and judged against.

target_lufs.description: Programme loudness the final mp4 is normalised to.

true_peak_max_dbtp.description: Highest true peak the normalised mix may reach.
true_peak_max_dbtp.x-hazard: Four times oversampling under-reads a true peak and the AAC encode overshoots on top of that, so a ceiling above about -1 dBTP reports a clean mix that clips on a listener's decoder.

range_max_lu.description: Widest loudness range the normalised mix may hold.

motion.description: These keys decide how much motion a build renders, which changes the film it produces.

reduce.description: Render every slide as the reduced-motion variant, which is the film a viewer who asks for less motion should be given.
reduce.x-range: takes any value of its type

scale.description: Multiplier on every declared motion span and duration in the deck.
scale.x-hazard: A scale above one slows motion down, and a span slowed past the measurable ceiling makes its own cue unmeasurable, so each scaled span is clamped at that ceiling rather than obeyed.

elevenlabs.description: These keys point at the ElevenLabs API and size its soundscape requests.

api_base.description: Base URL of the ElevenLabs API.
api_base.x-range: takes any value of its type

sound_model.description: Model for ambience and sound effect requests. A soundscape table can name its own.
sound_model.x-range: takes any value of its type

music_model.description: Model for music requests. A soundscape table can name its own.
music_model.x-range: takes any value of its type

music_bitrate.description: Bitrate of the music file that `soundscape` joins from its chunks.

max_music_chunk_seconds.description: Longest music request. Longer music is requested in chunks and crossfaded.

ambience_seconds.description: Length of a generated ambience bed. A soundscape table can set `duration_seconds` instead.

ambience_prompt_influence.description: Prompt influence of an ambience request. A soundscape table can set its own.

effect_seconds.description: Length of a generated sound effect. A soundscape table can set `duration_seconds` instead.

effect_prompt_influence.description: Prompt influence of a sound effect request. A soundscape table can set its own.

timeout_seconds.description: Seconds before a sound or music request times out.

output.description: These keys switch the files a build writes beside the final mp4 and how long they are kept.

timestamped_copy.description: Write a second copy of the final mp4 named with the date and time.
timestamped_copy.x-range: takes any value of its type

events_keep_runs.description: How many runs of event files `build/events/` keeps before the oldest is deleted.

tools.description: These keys name the tools DeckTalk drives, for a machine that supplies its own.

ffmpeg.description: ffmpeg executable. It is empty for the build DeckTalk fetches itself.
ffmpeg.x-range: takes any value of its type

ffprobe.description: ffprobe executable. It is empty for the build DeckTalk fetches itself.
ffprobe.x-range: takes any value of its type

cache_dir.description: Directory the fetched Chromium and ffmpeg builds live in. It is empty for the standard per-user cache.
cache_dir.x-range: takes any value of its type

host.description: These keys are facts about this machine that a run measures rather than a person chooses.

presentation_bias_ms.description: How long this machine takes to present a frame the page has already drawn, which is what a run's own measurements of this machine are read against.
presentation_bias_ms.x-hazard: A bias written by hand is a claim about this machine that nobody measured, and the one command that can measure it is beside this key. It is measured or it is zero.

project.description: The film itself: its name, its deck and the files it is built from.

section.description: One section of the script, in the order the film plays them.

items.description: One section of the script, in the order the film plays them.

transition.description: How one section is joined to the next.

soundscape.description: The music, the ambience and the sound effects a run generates.

x-numbers.description: Derived: a quarter-size frame is what every share is measured over, at every frame size.
Derived: a quarter-size frame is what every share is measured over, at every frame size.
Derived: one pixel per H.264 transform block, so the block average cancels the encoder's ringing at every frame size rather than only at 1080p.
Derived: one pixel per H.264 transform block, as the block width is.
Derived: the reference frame has to sit outside the window the offset limit allows, or the check compares a cue against a frame the same cue had already changed.
Truth: the rate the recorder captures at, which DeckTalk cannot set and so never asks for.
Truth: the H.264 transform block the block-averaged copy of a frame cancels ringing over.
Truth: half a frame of rounding guard on each side of the window the offset limit allows.
Calibration: the runtime's own reporting floor, under which a frame gap cannot be seen.
Truth: the level DeckTalk generates its own click at, which every click floor sits under.
Truth: the span at which an effect covers its own cue, which is the ceiling every declared span, every scaled span and every staggered total is held under.
